arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Wed Nov 25 (midpoint): Lior let Haifa slip at 12:40; Dana: 'say something real', he gave her an aphid update, said congratulations twice and walked off. 21:35 her text: can they talk properly Friday? Typed, deleted. Thu Nov 26: bad coffee at home, he says 'stay' to a pretend barista in improv, then texts Dana 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Next: week 3 he stays away from Cafe Nahat; Noa calls it disappearing. Sun Dec 6 he says it plainly.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: 'Thursday payment run confirmed!!'. Thu Nov 26: the run 'went out', Sababa's batch is Monday; Ishai asks for Monday before ten in writing and refuses the Hebrew banner until then. Next: week 3 Gadi asks for January and Ishai gets angry for the first time.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Wed Nov 25: Pump House with Ishai, 'people leave, and it's not about you', 'it's nobody' on her buzzing phone, Saturday dinner, no plumbers. Thu Nov 26: she skips the night out, 'tired'. Next: Sat Nov 28 after havdalah he finds out, and for once takes care of her.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi and Eli
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26 (reveal): over Ishai's burnt coffee she admits it: Eli last came four years ago in March, for Yitzhak's seventieth; 'busy' is so she doesn't say 'far'. She makes Ishai promise not to call Eli. He promises not to CALL. Next: week 3 he quietly messages Eli; Eli lands Mon Nov 30.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26 (reveal): no proverb at lunch; Ishai asks, Avi shows the envelope: the landlord doubles the rent from January, eleven years on this corner. 'Wanting isn't rent.' Next: week 4 a sufganiyot queue round the block; open.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26, lesson 4, the last Noa paid for: in a scene with a barista who is leaving he says 'I want you to stay' and 'I'll learn the timetable'. He signs up for the next course (from Dec 10) at full price, himself. Yael: 'now the real one'.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Wed Nov 25: Lior let Haifa slip and called himself a fool; 'chapter fifteen is ruined'. Moshe: fewer aphids. Next: Sun Nov 29 Ishai reads chapter one for the cover and recognises himself.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26: the night out at The Black Candle with Ishai; he notices too much about Noa ('since we were fourteen'), reads 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' over Ishai's shoulder. Saturday: PixelPlex with Ishai (A Midsummer Night's Dream, engine). Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: First night Mon Nov 23: 91 up. Tue Nov 24 Ishai lent Yossi 200, 'don't tell Boaz'. Next: second night Mon Dec 7, Yossi pays back in coins.

beats.goal: Week 3 begins: instead of going to Cafe Nahat, Ishai makes his own coffee at home and burns it. Mrs. Levi knocks for her honey-cake plate and stays for a cup she sweetens three times. Ishai, as Moti told him yesterday, asks her how long since Eli came. She admits it: four years in March, for Yitzhak's seventieth; she says 'busy' so she doesn't have to say 'far'. She turns it on him (why is he home making poison instead of at his cafe?) and makes him promise not to call Eli. He promises not to call.
beats.teaser: Mrs. Levi comes for her plate. Ishai finally asks how long.
beats.forceText: Over Ishai's burnt coffee, Mrs. Levi admits Eli hasn't visited in four years. She makes him promise not to call him.

forceLines.say: Four years in March. Busy is easier to say than far.
I promise. I won't call him.

forceCommentary.say: Four years. And she said 'busy' every single time. My heart.
He promised not to call. He said nothing about typing.

moments.text: Ishai stands at the counter with a small pot of coffee that has clearly boiled over. A knock: Mrs. Levi in her robe, here for her honey-cake plate. She sniffs the air before she says hello.

lines.say: Motek. Something is burning. Is it you?
It's coffee. Mostly coffee.
Since when you make coffee at home?
Since today. It's cheaper.
You have a cafe. With a girl who draws leaves.
Your plate. Washed. Want a cup?
If I faint, tell Moti it was your coffee.
Sugar?
Three. No, four. It needs help.
Did Eli see the candle photo?
Two blue ticks now. Blue! He saw it.
And?
And he's busy. Toronto is a busy city.
Mrs. Levi... how long since he came?
Who told you to ask that? Moti.
Nobody. Me. I'm asking.

commentary.say: Four sugars. She's not drinking the coffee, she's negotiating with it.
Two BLUE ticks. He saw it. Eli, I'm coming to Toronto.

then.text: They sit at the kitchen island with the bitter coffee; Mrs. Levi stirs and stirs, looking at Moshe on the sill instead of at Ishai.

moments.text: Mrs. Levi puts the spoon down. Falafel lays his head on her slipper. She answers the question at last, quietly, to the cup.

lines.say: Four years. In March.
Four years?
Yitzhak's seventieth. Eli fixed the stair light with him.
The one he broke at twelve.
Ha. You remember. Moti tells everything.
So 'busy' is...
Busy is easier to say than far.
Do you want him to come?
At my age you don't want. You wait.
Waiting is just wanting with no sound.
Ooh. Your little class. And you?
Me what?
Why are you here making poison and not at your cafe?
...It's cheaper.
Liar. Promise me one thing. Don't call Eli.
Mrs. Levi—
Promise. I'm not a project.
I promise. I won't call him.

commentary.say: 'Busy is easier to say than far.' Somebody get this woman a better son.
He promised not to CALL. I've read contracts. That's a loophole.

update.memory: Told Ishai the truth over his terrible coffee: Eli last came four years ago, for Yitzhak's seventieth. Made him promise not to call. He's hiding from his cafe girl.

beats.goal: Thursday, the promised payment run. Gadi phones all cheer: the run went out! Just not to Ishai: Sababa's freelancer batch is Monday, the bank's new system. Ishai, for the first time, holds a line: Monday before ten, in writing, and no Hebrew version of the banner until the money lands. Gadi steals his own phrase back: 'Yes, and!'. Not angry yet, only firm. After the call Ishai writes MONDAY 10:00 on a sticky note on the laptop and opens Ruti's email, still in drafts.
beats.teaser: Thursday's payment run. Gadi calls with good news, mostly.
beats.forceText: Gadi phones: the payment run went out, but Ishai's batch is Monday. Ishai asks for Monday before ten in writing.

forceLines.say: The run went out! Your batch is Monday. Small detail.
Monday before ten. In writing. Then the Hebrew banner.

forceCommentary.say: A payment run that runs past you. Innovative banking.
He said 'in writing'. Gadi, be afraid. Slightly.

moments.text: Ishai is at his desk with the cold half of the burnt coffee when the phone rings: GADI SABABA. He puts him on speaker and sits up straight.

lines.say: Ishai! Thursday! The payment run went out!
It did? Great. Thank you.
Went out, flying, beautiful. Big morning.
I don't see anything yet.
Right, so, small detail. Freelancers are the second batch.
Second batch is when?
Monday. The bank's new system. Very modern.
You said Thursday. In writing.
And Thursday it ran! Just not to you.
Gadi. Monday before ten. Write it to me.
Before ten, sure, before eleven, we're family—
Before ten.
Okay. Okay! Ten. Also, tiny thing—
No.
You don't know what it is!
The banner in Hebrew. After Monday.
Ha! Yes, and! You're learning, my friend.
That's my line, Gadi.

commentary.say: He said NO before the tiny thing. Thursday's lesson started early.
'Very modern.' The bank. Gadi's excuses come with a design brief now.

then.text: Ishai hangs up and stares at the banner file on the screen without touching it, tapping a pen on the desk.

update.memory: Told Ishai the run went out but his batch is Monday. He wanted Monday before ten in writing and refused the Hebrew banner until then. New Ishai.

moments.text: Ishai writes MONDAY 10:00 on a yellow sticky note and presses it on the laptop's edge. He opens his email: Ruti's message, his reply still in drafts. He reads it twice and doesn't send.

lines.say: Monday. Ten. That's a real time, Moshe.
And you... you stay in drafts. For now.

commentary.say: The Ruti draft. It's been in there so long it pays rent.
A sticky note with a deadline. This is Ishai's version of a lawyer.

beats.goal: Lunch at Avi's kiosk. Avi serves him without a single proverb, slow and distracted, a brown envelope under the napkins. Ishai notices and, Thursday style, asks plainly instead of politely. Avi tells him: the landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January; eleven years on this corner. 'Wanting isn't rent.' Ishai offers to help and doesn't know how; Avi tells him to eat. No solution today.
beats.teaser: Avi's kiosk, lunch. No proverb today. Ishai notices.
beats.forceText: At the kiosk Avi admits the landlord is doubling his rent from January. Ishai doesn't know how to help yet.

forceLines.say: Double. From January. Eleven years on this corner.
What do you want to do?

forceCommentary.say: No proverb. That was the clue. I hate being right.
Double rent for a falafel kiosk. Tel Aviv found a new way to be Tel Aviv.

moments.text: Midday on Herzl Street, Falafel tied to the kiosk's leg. Avi fills a pita slowly, too slowly, a brown envelope sticking out under the napkin box. Ishai eats standing at the counter.

lines.say: Pita. Extra amba. Like always.
Thanks. No proverb today?
Proverbs are free. Nothing is free this week.
That sounds like a proverb.
Then I owe you nothing. Eat.
You put in pickles. I hate pickles.
...Yes. Sorry. Give it.
Avi. You know eleven years I hate pickles.
Eleven years. Yes. Eleven.
You said it twice.
Old men repeat. Like the radio.
Is it the envelope? Under the napkins.
Envelope, napkins. You see too much.
I'm learning to ask. Thursdays.
Your clown class.
Improv. So I'm asking. What's in it?

commentary.say: Pickles for Ishai. After eleven years. Something is badly wrong in the kiosk.
Look at Ishai asking a direct question. I'm going to cry into my amba.

then.text: Avi makes a new pita without pickles and pushes it over; Ishai eats while Avi wipes the same patch of counter again and again.

moments.text: Avi slides the envelope out and lays it flat on the counter between the tahini and the salt, so Ishai can read the landlord's letterhead without Avi having to say it.

lines.say: The landlord. From January, double.
Double? The whole rent?
Double. He says the street is 'going up'.
The street's the same street.
The street is the same. The price is not.
Eleven years on this corner.
Eleven. Your whole building eats here.
What do you want to do?
I want to stay. Wanting isn't rent.
Can I help? A sign, a menu, a—
A logo won't pay a landlord, motek.
Then something else. I'll think.
Don't think. Eat. And don't tell Mrs. Levi.
Why not?
She'll cook for me. I'll get fat and still pay double.
Your secret's safe. Mostly.

commentary.say: 'Wanting isn't rent.' Avi just wrote this season's theme song.
First Eli, now the kiosk. Ishai's collecting secrets like Moti collects coins.

update.memory: Showed Ishai the landlord's letter: double rent from January. Told him wanting isn't rent and a logo won't pay. He wants to help. Don't tell Mrs. Levi.

beats.goal: Improv lesson 4, the last one Noa paid for: saying what you want, with nobody helping. Yael sets a scene: she is a barista closing her little cafe for the last time, moving north; he is the regular. Ishai freezes, says 'congratulations', and Yael stops him: congratulations is a door you close. Again: he says 'I want you to stay', and 'yes, and if you go, I'll learn the train timetable'. The class claps. Then Yael asks him to say what he wants as himself, no character. After class on the street she says that was the last lesson Noa paid for; he signs up for the next course at full price, himself. 'Now say it to the real one.' 'Friday. Maybe.'
beats.teaser: Last improv lesson. Ishai has to say what he wants.
beats.forceText: Improv lesson 4: in a scene with a barista who is leaving, Ishai says 'I want you to stay'. He pays for the next course himself.

forceLines.say: Congratulations is a door you close. Again.
I want you to stay. That's it. That's the whole thing.

forceCommentary.say: He said stay. To a pretend barista. Babe, the real one has a phone.
Full price for the next course. Gadi could never.

moments.text: The back of The Black Candle, tables against the walls, the class in a half circle of chairs. Yael puts a coffee cup on a bar stool: the counter. She calls Ishai up first.

lines.say: Lesson four. The last one. Today nobody helps you.
Nobody helped me before either.
I helped a lot. You didn't notice. Up.
Up. Okay. What am I?
A regular. Same cafe every day. I'm the barista.
...Of course you are.
Today is my last day. I'm moving north. Go.
Hi. Um. Congratulations. That's big. Not bad.
Thanks. One last coffee?
Yes. Sorry. Yes. Congratulations.

commentary.say: She said north. He said congratulations. Twice. We've seen this episode.
Yael, do you have a camera in Cafe Nahat? Because WOW.

moments.text: Yael raises a hand and the scene stops. A few people in the half circle laugh, kindly. Ishai stands holding the empty cup.

lines.say: Stop. You said congratulations twice.
It's polite. She's happy.
Congratulations is a door you close. Softly. But closed.
So what do I say?
What do you want? Not what's polite. Want.
I don't know.
You know. You're holding the cup like it's a bird.
...Okay.
Again. Last day. I'm moving north.
Hi. One last coffee. And... wait.

commentary.say: 'Holding the cup like it's a bird.' Yael sees everything. I'm scared of her.
He said 'wait'. In Ishai, that's a speech.

moments.text: The room goes quiet. Ishai puts the cup down on the stool and looks at Yael, then at the floor, then back at Yael.

lines.say: Wait for what?
I don't want you to go.
Louder. The cafe has a coffee machine. It's loud.
I want you to stay.
And if I still go?
Yes, and... I'll learn the train timetable.
The train?
Every week. I'll sit by the window. I'll bring the plant.
What plant?
...There's a plant. It's a long story. I want you to stay. That's it.

commentary.say: 'I'll learn the train timetable.' I'm on the floor. Someone send this to Haifa.
He brought Moshe into a fictional scene. The basil has range.

moments.text: The half circle claps. Yael doesn't let him sit. She takes the cup away so his hands are empty.

lines.say: Good. Now no character. Ishai. What do you want?
Me? Here?
Here. One sentence. No sorry.
I want... to stop saying congratulations to things I hate.
Good. And?
And to say it to the real person. Not a cup.
That's homework. The only homework.
Can I sit now?
Sit. Before you apologise.
I wasn't going to... thank you.

commentary.say: 'Congratulations to things I hate.' Four lessons, and that's the sentence.
Homework: say it to the real person. Dana, keep your phone charged.

moments.text: After class on Herzl Street, the light going orange. Yael rolls a cigarette she won't light; Ishai holds his jacket instead of wearing it.

lines.say: That was the last lesson Noa paid for.
I know. She told me. Twice.
New course from December tenth. Four fifty.
I'll take it. I'll pay. Myself.
Friends discount? Noa would ask for one.
No. Full price. Full price is the point.
Ha. Who are you?
I'm working on it.
And the real one? The barista?
She's not moving. Not yet. Maybe.
When will you tell her?
Friday. She asked for Friday.
Friday is a day. Days come.
That's terrifying, Yael.
Yes. And?

commentary.say: Friday! He said Friday! I'm booking a dress for Friday.
Full price. He paid full price. Somebody frame that receipt.

update.memory: Lesson 4: in the barista scene he said 'I want you to stay' and the train timetable. Signed up for the next course, full price, himself. Says he'll tell the real one Friday.

beats.goal: Thursday night out at The Black Candle with Tomer (Noa texts she's too tired to come). Ishai tells Tomer about the barista scene and 'I want you to stay'; Tomer: say it to the real one. Ishai asks about Noa's 'nobody' calls; Tomer notices too much about her ('since we were fourteen'), a hint of his own secret, and quickly changes the subject. Then, while Tomer orders, Ishai finally answers Dana's text: 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Tomer reads it over his shoulder: 'You wrote sorry. You're not busy.' Ishai pulls back anyway. The night goes on.
beats.teaser: Night out with Tomer. Dana's text finally gets an answer.
beats.forceText: At The Black Candle with Tomer, Ishai finally answers Dana: 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Tomer reads it over his shoulder.

forceLines.say: You wrote sorry. You're not busy, Ishai.

forceCommentary.say: Four hours ago he said 'stay' out loud. Now 'busy, sorry'. I need a minute.
Tomer read it over his shoulder. The only honest witness in this bar.

moments.text: The Black Candle, Thursday, loud guitars low. Tomer comes back from the bar with two beers. Ishai's phone buzzes on the table first: a text from Noa.

message.say: Can't come tonight, sorry, dead tired. Tell me about class tomorrow? Saturday still on. No plumbers.

lines.say: Noa's not coming. 'Dead tired'.
Noa? Tired? Noa doesn't get tired.
That's what I said.
Fine. More beer for us. So? Last lesson?
I said 'I want you to stay'.
To who?!
To Yael. She was a barista. Moving north.
Yael was a... oh. OH.
It was an exercise.
It was a rehearsal, my friend.
The whole class clapped.
Of course they clapped. Did you say it to Dana?
Friday. She wants to talk Friday.
And you answered her?
...Not yet.
Twenty-four hours, Ishush. That's a long 'not yet'.

commentary.say: He said it to the wrong barista! Close, babe. Same job, wrong woman.
Noa, 'dead tired', on a Thursday. Noa doesn't do tired. Noted.

then.text: They drink and watch a man at the bar argue with the jukebox; Tomer keeps glancing at Noa's text on Ishai's phone.

moments.text: Halfway down the second beer. Ishai turns his phone face down. Tomer picks at the label of his bottle.

lines.say: Can I ask you something? About Noa.
Ask. I'm an open pipe.
Her phone keeps ringing. She says it's nobody.
Nobody calls a lot lately.
You noticed too?
I've known Noa since we were fourteen.
I know.
When she's fine, she's quiet. She hasn't been quiet in a month.
You notice a lot about her.
Somebody has to. You're busy with baristas.
That's fair.
Ask her Saturday. Properly. Not like you.
What's like me?
You ask, she says great, you say great. Great.
And you? You never ask her?
Me? I'm the loud one. Nobody tells the loud one. Another beer?

commentary.say: 'Somebody has to.' Tomer, that's not a friend sentence. That's a fourteen-year sentence.
Since they were FOURTEEN. Tomer, babe, your face just did a whole thing.

moments.text: Tomer goes to the bar. Ishai turns the phone over, opens Dana's message, types fast and sends before he can delete. Tomer comes back, leans over his shoulder and reads it.

lines.say: What did you send? Show me.
It's nothing. I answered her.
'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Ishai.
It's an answer.
You wrote sorry. You're not busy.
I am now.
Busy with what? Moshe?
With... not doing this on Friday.
Four hours ago you said 'stay' to a stranger.
That was a cup. This is real.
That's the point of the cup, idiot.
If I see her Friday, she tells me she's going.
And if you don't, she goes anyway.
Then at least I didn't hear it.
That's not a no, that's a hide.
Drink your beer, Tomer.
I'm drinking. I'm also disappointed. I can do both.

commentary.say: 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' He said STAY four hours ago. I'm throwing my headset.
'That's not a no, that's a hide.' Tomer, electrician, philosopher, correct.

update.memory: Thursday night out. Ishai said 'stay' in class, then texted Dana 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Told him that's hiding. Noa's 'nobody' calls worry me. Didn't say why.

hook.text: In class he said 'I want you to stay.' Then he texted Dana 'Busy Friday. Sorry.' Who will call it what it is?

previously.text: Lior let Haifa slip before one; Dana asked for something real and got an aphid update. Her text: talk properly Friday? He typed, deleted, and slept on it.

hosts: Thursday. Week three. Dana's text from last night is still sitting there, read and unanswered.
'Can we talk properly Friday?' Nine words. He has drafted eleven replies. All deleted.
No coffee from Cafe Nahat this morning. He's brewing at home. Somebody check the smoke alarm.
Moshe looks better. Fewer aphids. One of them is clearly doing better than Ishai.
Last improv lesson today. The one Noa paid for. Yael doesn't do easy finales.
Moti told him to ask Mrs. Levi one question today. Just one. 'How long.'
Gadi promised a Thursday payment run. It's Thursday. We'll see what runs.
Avi's been on the phone at the back of the kiosk all week. No proverbs since Monday.
Twelve days until December seventh. Dana has a decision. Ishai has a sticky-note habit.
If you're just joining us: Haifa, a barista, a basil, and a man who says congratulations.
Falafel walked twice yesterday so Ishai could avoid one conversation. Dog of the year.
Thursday is night-out day. Last week he bet fifty shekels on Eilat. Haifa was not on his list.
Mrs. Levi's in her robe again. Robe days are honest days in this building.
Noa said 'people leave, and it's not about you'. She wasn't talking about Dana.
Lior hasn't written a word since yesterday. Chapter fifteen is officially in mourning.
Small reminder: Saturday night is the PixelPlex. A Midsummer Night's Dream. Tomer's going.
Thirteen degrees this morning. He'll say it's warm. Dana says he gets cold when he's miserable.
Rule of the show: when Ishai cleans the counter twice, something's on his mind.
He hums when he's fine. He hasn't hummed since Tuesday.
Kobi's at the bar tonight from seven. By nine he'll have a lottery theory for Ishai's love life.
Noa's phone rings. Noa says nobody. Nobody has a very long ringtone.
Every sticky note on that laptop is a promise someone else made.
The kiosk smells the same. Avi doesn't sound the same. That's the clue, people.
Yael's homework last week: say no to someone you like. He did. To Noa. Small steps.
Today's forecast: clear skies, a cold evening, and at least one 'sorry'. Bet on it.
Tomer's been asking about Noa a lot lately. Just saying. Just noticing.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Thursday morning. Clear skies, thirteen degrees, everybody pretending it's not winter.
If you're making coffee at home today, our thoughts are with you.
Weekend's coming. Thursday is the Friday of people who work Fridays.
Clear tonight, chilly by the sea. Bring the jacket you always forget.
Traffic on Herzl is slow by the lights. Normal. Herzl has never been in a hurry.
A listener asks how to say a hard thing to someone. Our advice: before the song ends.
Next up, something slow, for anyone sitting at a counter alone.
Rents are up across the city again. Kiosks, cafes, everyone feels it.
Candles tomorrow at quarter past four. Plan your shopping, the market closes early.
Thursday night out? Be nice to the bartender. They remember everything.
Late tonight, cold and clear. Good night for walking home slowly.
Radio Herzl, still here, still slightly off the frequency, still yours.

zelig: The pigeons came early. Someone told them it's Thursday.
Four years is nothing for a tree. For a mother, it's long.
The bench is cold at both ends today. Fair.
You don't wait for bread. You go to the bakery.
michal: Thursday is leg day. Every day is leg day if you're brave.
Run club tomorrow at seven. I'm sending the reminder, not coming.
Mirror says form is fine. Mirror lies on Thursdays.
sivan: Six kilometres. Somebody beat that. Nobody will.
The guy with the hascii skipped. Again.
Incline twelve. Don't talk to me.
lior: Chapter fifteen. Delete. Chapter fifteen. Delete.
A man who apologises to his coffee... no. Too much. Keep it.
She said she'd tell him herself. I am a fool with a laptop.
Writers should never be allowed near real people.
Maybe chapter fifteen is about a coffee nobody drank.
kobi: Thursday. Lottery numbers come in threes on Thursdays.
Nine o'clock, second beer, the numbers are getting clearer.
Number eleven came again. Eleven is a sign. Of what, I'll know soon.
Midnight. I've solved everything. I'll forget by morning.

street: ...he said the street is going up, I said up where...
...my mother asks when I'm coming, I say soon, she says soon...
...bring a jacket, it's clear but it bites...
market: ...close early tomorrow, Shabbat, quarter past four...
...the challah's for tomorrow, today you get yesterday's price...
...three onions, not four, I'm not made of money...
park: ...the pigeons know him, they come before he sits...
...cold, but the sun is honest today...
cafe: ...the regular didn't come today, the quiet one...
...oat milk again, she won the war...
...who's going to draw the leaves if she goes...
...he left a coin yesterday and didn't drink it...

chat.say: Stair light paid, thank you all. Receipts in the mailboxes. Moti.
Who is burning coffee on the fourth floor? The whole stairwell smells like a station cafe.
The grey cats ate everything. Thank you to the young man on four. He makes terrible coffee.
Bus 88 detour by the lights this afternoon. Boaz says don't ask him why.
Reminder: no bicycles in the entrance. Yes, this means the red one.
Anyone have a spare challah tray for tomorrow? Mine became a cat bed.
Candles tomorrow at 16:16. Who wants honey cake? I made too much. Again.
Someone left the stair light on all evening. Committee, we paid for it, not for that.
